title: Ops pocket rhythm and release snapshot — mini-calendar & checkpad
content:
Purpose: compact, on-shift reference for a small/medium release lane. Designed for a single on-call deck + two observers. Keep this at hand during the 48h window around the release.

Context and constraints:
- Release type: feature + infra (runtime kernel swap, batching tweaks). Non-breaking, but affects cold-start paths and KV cache behavior.
- Audience: release conductor, telemetry lead, infra on-call, two release shepherds.
- Goals: deploy with <5% error-rate deviation, steady p50 p95 token latency, zero customer-facing incidents.

Quick ownership map (who pings who):
- Conductor: Maya Patel (this doc owner) — overall go/no-go
- Telemetry: Elias Chen — dashboards, alert tuning
- Infra on-call: Jamila Ortiz — node-level issues, kernel fallback
- Rollback/Critical Fix PR lead: Noah Rivera — hotfix gating and fast rollback patch

Preflight checklist (T-48h to T-1h) — short actionable items (tick when done):
- [ ] Dependency freeze: confirm all runtime PRs merged and pinned (REL-1482).
- [ ] Canary harness ready: traffic split script in /ops/harness and smoke suite invoked.
- [ ] Dashboard snapshot: save pre-release baseline (latency, errors, queue length).
- [ ] Alert thresholds prepped: lower sensitivity for rollout window (see telemetry notes).
- [ ] Capacity plan: reserved burst for 2x expected QPS, autoscaler cooldowns set.
- [ ] Secrets/keys: validate KMS access and no env drift in private clusters.
- [ ] Communication: calendar invites to release-runway, #release-runway pinned message with schedule and links.
- [ ] Rollout PR described: release notes, user-facing summary, and downgrade steps included in PR description.

Mini-calendar (compact 48h view)
- Day -2 (T-48h): final smoke run in staging, perf harness on 1h steady-state run, preflight retro with leads.
- Day -1 (T-24h): production dry-run of smoke (0% traffic), load test on dedicated lane, snapshot dashboards, open go/no-go thread.
- Day 0 (T0 + 0h): start 5% pilot in eu-west for 30m. If green, escalate to 15% for 30m. If green, 35% for 1h.
- Day 0 (T0 + 2.5h): if all signals good, global push to 60% then monitor 2h before 100% by automated cadence.
- Day 1 (T+24h): retention checks, quality regression tests over sample prompts, run long-tail error sweep.
- Day 2 (T+48h): postmortem notes draft, mark any 'to-fix' tickets, finalize release notes.

Rollout cadence & pause points (hard gates):
- Gate A (after 5% 30m): no >2x baseline p95 latency, error rate <1.5x baseline. Otherwise pause and assess (10m investigation window).
- Gate B (after 15% 30m): stable p50/p95, no queue growth >15%.
- Gate C (after 35% 60m): no downstream saturation, no change to SLO error budget burn.
- Gate D (before global 100%): business metrics sanity check (short sampling of production queries for regressions).

Telemetry probes (essential signals to watch live):
- Ingress QPS and per-model throughput (control: pre-release snapshot).
- Token p50/p95 latency by region and model.
- Error rates: 5xx by service, user-facing error % by route.
- KV cache hit ratio and cold-start count (this release affects cache warming).
- Node GPU utilization and Memory reserved vs freed.
- Queue depth and batch sizes (unexpected batching drops cause latency spikes).
- Sampled text outputs (quality smoke) — random 1k requests flagged to QA.

Smoke test matrix (to run automatically at each gate):
- Auth & routing: token validation, tenant routing, fallback model path.
- Generation: short sequence, mid sequence, long tail generation (check for truncation or hallucination regressions).
- Streaming: connection stability for long streams, resume behavior.
- Embeddings: vector size sanity checks, embedding divergence threshold.

Rollback triggers and fast rollback plan (if any trigger fires):
- Trigger list (anyone may call rollback):
  - sustained p95 > 2x baseline for >30m
  - error budget burn >10% in 15m
  - emergent 5xx cascade affecting >3% of requests
  - data integrity suspicion on routed customer (immediate stop)
- Fast rollback steps:
  1) Conductor declares rollback on #release-runway and page infra on-call.
  2) Execute traffic revert in routing layer to previous stable model (route snapshot id in PR).
  3) If revert fails, reimage affected nodes using snapshot AMI (infra playbook link).
  4) Open hotfix PR for regression and tag REL-HOTFIX in Jira.

Communication script (short messages to send at gate boundaries):
- At T0 start: "Release starting: kernel-swap + batching tweak. Lane: eu-west pilot 5%. Leads: Maya, Elias, Jamila. Channel: #release-runway."
- On Gate pass: "Gate X passed — moving to Y%: key signals stable (latency p95: X ms, errors: Y%)."
- On Gate pause: "Pausing at Gate X due to [signal]. Investigating — paging [owner]. Do not escalate traffic changes until cleared."
- On rollback: "Rolling back release: route reverted to snapshot <id>. Postmortem ticket: REL-1482. Follow-up owners assigned."

Release notes draft (short, user-facing) — put in PR description later:
- Summary: "April runtime update: improved batching kernel selection and KV cache warm paths. Expected benefits: lower per-token cost for mid-long sequences, reduced tail latency for multi-turn chat."
- Changes: "Runtime: kernel selector v2.1, KV cache preheat hook enabled, optimized batching heuristics for seq >2048."
- Impact: "No breaking API changes. Possible slight cold-start increase for very small payloads during first 10s after node spin-up — mitigated by cache preheat. Observability change: new metrics kv_cache_warm_count and kernel_selector_election_time."
- Rollout plan: "Staged rollout over 48h with telemetry gates; immediate rollback plan in place."
- Action for customers: "No action required. Contact support@redwood.ai if you see degraded outputs or increased latencies beyond historical norms."

Post-release (T+24 to T+72h) checklist: 
- [ ] Validate final dashboards against baseline and tag long-tail anomalies.
- [ ] Move any follow-up bugs to sprint board and assign severity/owner.
- [ ] Revert alert sensitivity to normal and document temporary thresholds used.
- [ ] Draft brief postmortem (fields: timeline, root cause if any, mitigation).
- [ ] Close go/no-go thread in Slack and publish release notes on confluence + changelog.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need a small harness to auto-sample outputs and run a light QA scoring function (ask ML infra team).
- Confirm that kernel fallback path is exercised in staging — Jamila to create canary that forces alternate kernel.
- Decide whether to expose kv_cache_warm_count to customer metrics (privacy/volume tradeoff).

Useful links & ops snippets:
- Traffic split CLI: ops/traffic-split.sh --lane eu-west --pct <n> (use safe flags --dry-run to rehearse).
- Dashboard links: confluence:Release-Prep-Apr-2027#dashboards (direct links pinned in Slack).
- Rollback quick command: ops/revert-route --snapshot-id <id> --env prod

Notes: keep this doc short and pinned. Save a trimmed copy into the release PR as a release-play-summary. If anything deviates from the cadence above, capture it in the go/no-go thread with timestamps.

Session log (skeleton — fill during live ops):
- 2027-04-12 09:00 Maya: kicked off preflight smoke (staging).
- 2027-04-12 11:30 Elias: dashboard snapshot saved, minor p95 blip during 20m window (investigating).
- 2027-04-13 08:00 Jamila: infra dry-run passed, kernel fallback exercised.
- 2027-04-13 12:15 Maya: pilot started 5% eu-west.

(end of doc)
